text:
emma: Heads up — nightly-archiver ran for tenant-archive-bucket and some snapshots uploaded w/o cmek metadata. Noticed while looking at retention audit :eyes:
raj: Do we mean the x-amz-server-side-encryption header missing or the kmsKeyId on the snapshot metadata?
emma: kmsKeyId missing. Objects have SSE-S3 set but no x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id header/metadata. Started a small script to list objects: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket tenant-archive-bucket --query 'Contents[].Key' | xargs -n1 -I{} aws s3api head-object --bucket tenant-archive-bucket --key '{}'`
maria: @emma can you paste sample key and head-object output? Also any recent RBAC changes to the archival service account?
emma: sample: `tenant/2025-03-12/tenant-42-snap-20250312.tar.gz` head-object: `{"ServerSideEncryption":"AES256"}` — no KMS key fields.
luis: We rolled a policy change last week that removed iam:Encrypt on cmk for `archival-runner@project` while we were troubleshooting access. Might be related.
oliver: If service couldn't use CMK, S3 probably defaulted to SSE-S3. That means objects are encrypted by AWS-managed keys, not customer CMK. Restore still possible but doesn't meet compliance.
raj: Immediate triage steps: 1) confirm which objects affected, 2) check CloudTrail for kms:GenerateDataKey failures or AccessDenied, 3) restore test for one object to verify contents decrypts, 4) audit-logs update + notif to compliance.
emma: On it. Ran CloudTrail query for `kms:GenerateDataKey` with Resource: arn:aws:kms:.../cmk-archive. Found 3 AccessDenied events around 2025-03-12 03:14 UTC referencing `archival-runner@project`. Screenshot attached (not in thread).
maria: :warning: This is a compliance issue for 4 tenants with regulatory flags. We need to: a) regrant Encrypt for archival-runner, b) re-ingest affected snapshots using cmek, c) create compensating controls & timeline for audit.
oliver: Regranting is ok but we should rotate the CMK or create a new one to re-encrypt moving forward. Also add a guard in archiver: abort if CMK encrypt fails (currently falls back to SSE-S3).
luis: I can push a quick IAM patch to re-add kms:Encrypt + kms:GenerateDataKey for the specific key and principal. Will open a PR and ping @emma for verification.
emma: Please include a condition restricting to the archiver principal and bucket ARN. Also set `kms:ViaService` and `aws:SourceAccount` conditions.
raj: For audit logging: we should add an automated weekly check that ensures head-object contains `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id` for objects in archive-bucket older than 24h. Add an alert to #eng-oncall if >0.
maria: Compliance wants a timeline and proof: list of affected object keys, CT events, remediation plan, and a restore verification runbook.
emma: I'll assemble artifacts. Estimated 2-3 hours to enumerate and re-ingest small batch, longer for full re-encrypt. tagging @encops-bot to create incident ticket.
encops-bot: Incident created: INC-20250312-archiver-cmek-miss. Assignees: @luis, @emma, @maria. SLA: 72h.
oliver: Post-mortem action items: prevent silent fallback, add unit test for CMK availability in archiver CI, and ensure deploy RBAC changes require tech lead + security approval.
maria: Agree. Also recommend running a one-off kms:ListGrants audit across all service accounts monthly.
luis: PR opened: #4321 — regranting Encrypt for archival-runner with conditions. Link: https://git.internal/r/4321
emma: Verified after PR deploy — new uploads show `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id`. Re-ingesting keys for 4 tenants underway. Will post results.
raj: :thumbsup: Thanks team. Keep Compliance in the loop.
